informational_history.summary: External review found real soundness issues; this remains historical evidence, not an automatic counter input. The two original review reports are not retained in the current worktree and are owner-maintained outside the repo.
Step 7 evaluator attachability was consolidated with Step 6 after V29-V31 sibling bypasses.
Runtime-cache and source-digest findings remained algorithmic/proof-obligation risks.
V37-V46 findings showed that repo-derived receipt/report/Git authority was becoming its own attack surface.
V47-V50 closed strict-JSON receipt clean-counter state-machine false-ready paths, motivating removal of automatic repo-derived clean counting.
The repo no longer auto-counts clean reviews or auto-opens P1.3 from receipts. Owner manual decision is the only P1.3 entry authority.

V53-V56 found sibling findings in exact-safe BendersCut replay: strict evidence parsing, strict conflict/condition integer payloads, unresolved conflict member dilution, and aliasing conflict members that could strengthen a multi-member nogood into a one-literal ban.

Certified cut replay faithfulness is now an explicit P1.2 proof obligation. Future reviews should start from this anchor and look for remaining payload-coercion, missing-member, aliasing, condition-resolution, or apply/register atomicity bypasses.

V57-V60 were sibling findings in the same certified cut replay/domain faithfulness family: condition-required cuts, strict condition-key grammar and metadata consistency, current candidate-domain membership, and the actual full master-domain contract.
Certified exact runs must persist and validate an explicit full unfiltered master-domain contract, or fail closed before master construction when experimental domain-slicing knobs are present.

V61 found sibling certified lifecycle blockers after the V60 master-domain patch: pose-bool master and power-pole slot env overrides could change the actual constructed master domain, while EXACT_OUTER_SKIP_UNKNOWN could turn a candidate-subset or best-effort outer campaign into full-domain certified evidence. The gate remains manual/fail-closed, but future reviews should start from the V61 master-domain plus candidate-frontier contract.

V62 found sibling/order certified lifecycle blockers after V61: candidate-level incumbents could survive UNKNOWN/max-attempt partial-frontier stops as terminal certified evidence, outer_search precheck paths could construct sessions under unsafe master-domain env before the V61 guard, and best_effort resume exhaustion could write certified-looking artifacts before manifest fail-closed. Future reviews should start from the V62 terminal frontier evidence and outer master-domain guard contract.

V63 found sibling certified lifecycle blockers after V62: EXACT_MASTER_GHOST_ANCHOR_FILTER was not included in the centralized pre-session unsafe master-domain env guard, and resume/import, manifest, inspector/report, and B5A wrapper export paths could still expose stale or contradictory CERTIFIED surfaces without terminal full-frontier evidence. Future reviews should start from the V63 terminal evidence export-boundary contract.

V64 found a sibling certified lifecycle blocker after V63: power-witness representation env knobs such as EXACT_LAZY_POWER_COMPLETION, EXACT_POWER_PLACEMENT_SUBPROBLEM, and its forensic bypass could change certified power evidence semantics before the centralized pre-session guard blocked them. Future reviews should start from the V64 power witness representation env guard contract.

V65/V66 found sibling certified lifecycle blockers after V64: additional power-witness encoding env knobs could alter the certified witness representation, direct ExactSearchSession construction had to block unsafe env before project load, unsafe-env blocks had to clear stale resumed terminal state, and terminal full-frontier evidence had to be committed before final_solution export.

The oversized certified cut replay obligation is split into four lifecycle compartments: cut replay, master-domain/witness representation, frontier terminal evidence, and export surface. Future reviews should start from this anchor and classify findings against those compartments.

V73 consolidated public CERTIFIED publication into src/search/certified_surface.py so the inspector, delivery manifest path, and B5A anchor wrapper consume one verifier verdict instead of local predicates.
V74 hardened the central certified-surface verifier so disk artifacts, strict JSON, recomputed exact hashes, and regular-file boundaries are authoritative over caller-supplied memory payloads.

V75 found that terminal CERTIFIED could still rely on a stop-reason string plus best certified candidate. It now requires replayable candidate-generation evidence, a safe-area-bound authority, status digest, and empty recomputed frontier before terminal/public certified publication.

V76 confirmed the central certified-surface verifier remains the public CERTIFIED gate and tightened pre-publication helpers so terminal full-frontier evidence must replay against the current project grid and authoritative safe-area bound before best_certified_result or manifest payloads can be produced.

V77 found a sibling writer seam after the central verifier review: direct delivery-manifest export could serialize best_certified_result from an in-memory campaign while the referenced disk checkpoint contained different state. The writer now requires exact JSON-equivalence to the regular in-project checkpoint before forming a certified manifest payload.

V78 found the remaining writer-publication seam after V77: raw manifest writes and caller-selected output_path could create certified-looking manifests outside the canonical public surface. Certified payloads with best_certified_result now require the canonical regular in-project data/solutions/certified_delivery_manifest.json output path and the guarded export writer.

V79 found two unsealed candidate-domain slicing axes in the V75 terminal-evidence validator: an exhausted max_aspect_ratio-sliced domain and an above-admissibility min_side (>6) domain both validated as authoritative full-frontier CERTIFIED while the filtered candidates were never refuted. Both axes are now rejected. The delivery-manifest deep validation also no longer skips the blueprint reverse-lookup for non-instance-shaped terminal placement solutions; it fails closed.

V80 closes the V79 residual and flips two enumerative defenses to deny-unknown. Terminal frontier evidence now includes project-level min_side admissibility and rejects unknown candidate_generation keys, stale v1 schema, min-side mismatches, and sub-admissible terminal final_result publication. certified_exact env overrides are checked by an allowlist: production operational knobs remain admitted, known proof-semantics knobs must stay canonical false/default, and future unclassified EXACT_* names fail closed.

V81 external review (first round after the V80 deny-unknown flip) found one algorithmic/soundness finding and one publication finding: F-01 mandatory-rectangle precheck consumers ignored partial_due_to_time_budget, so an infeasible anchor prefix could prune a candidate as INFEASIBLE; F-02 the single-base release builder accepted a run summary self-claiming CERTIFIED. Owner clean-streak count resets to 0.

V82 external review found two soundness findings, both locally reproduced end-to-end: F-1 the candidate domain canonicalized by h<=w while master feasibility is orientation-sensitive, so terminal full-frontier evidence proved exhaustion over half the domain (wrong published optimum demonstrated on a 3x3 toy); F-2 checkpoint/preloaded exact_safe_cuts entered the master after structural validation only, so a forged cut could prune the only feasible pose. Owner clean-streak count resets to 0.

V83 external review found three soundness findings, all locally reproduced: F-01 forged checkpoint with self-consistent terminal evidence published a geometrically impossible empty rectangle; F-02 whole-layout nogoods were escalated to candidate INFEASIBLE on the default coordinate-master path; F-03 the certified mandatory-instance loader silently shrank the instance set on malformed records. A reviewer-patch defect (ghost_pick counted as occupancy, which would have rejected every genuine terminal result) was caught and corrected during local landing. Owner clean-streak count resets to 0.

V84 external review found three soundness findings, all locally reproduced: the V83 witness scan proved existence but not optimality of the claimed empty rectangle; exact artifact hashing followed symlinks outside the project; and unknown extra instances in the terminal placement solution could forge occupancy blockers. All sealed fail-closed; the optimality scan is scoped to non-empty mandatory sets during landing. Owner clean-streak count resets to 0.

V85 external review found one soundness finding, locally reproduced: the terminal validator enforced mandatory coverage but not the generic_io-inferred required pose-level optionals, so a forged terminal checkpoint omitting the required protocol_storage_box published a CERTIFIED rectangle that is geometrically impossible once the box is placed. Sealed fail-closed. Owner clean-streak count resets to 0.

V86 external review found one soundness finding, locally reproduced with a master-level contradiction probe: the terminal validator never replayed power coverage, so a layout with a needs_power mandatory facility and no selected pole published as CERTIFIED while the certified master solved the same layout INFEASIBLE. Sealed fail-closed. Owner clean-streak count resets to 0.

V87 external review found two soundness findings, both locally reproduced: authorized-but-unforced power poles were counted as occupancy (letting a forged checkpoint flood cells and publish a smaller optimum), and final_result.ghost_rect anchor coordinates were never replayed (letting a blueprint publish a CERTIFIED rectangle on top of facilities). Sealed fail-closed. Owner clean-streak count resets to 0.

V88 external review found one soundness finding, locally reproduced: omitting ghost_rect.anchor_x/y bypassed the V87 anchor replay and published anchor=-1,-1 blueprints as CERTIFIED. The anchor is now protocol-required end to end. The reviewer patch broke the real-solver path (five downstream consumers treated the new ghost_pick marker as a facility); corrected during landing. Owner clean-streak count resets to 0.

V89 external review found one soundness finding, locally reproduced in both directions: the candidate record's ghost_pick provenance was never replayed, so forged checkpoints with a missing or tampered marker still published CERTIFIED. The binding is now fail-closed. Owner clean-streak count resets to 0.

V90 external review found one soundness finding, locally reproduced: arbitrary top-level final_result fields were projected into the public blueprint without any binding (forged belt routes published as CERTIFIED). The final_result shape is now a closed allowlist. Owner clean-streak count resets to 0.

V91 external review found one soundness finding, locally reproduced: the allowlisted final_result fields accepted forged nested keys (ghost_rect proof_status, search_stats proof_status) and contradictory mandatory metadata while the surface stayed publishable. Nested shapes are now closed. Owner clean-streak count resets to 0.

V92 external review found one soundness finding on the public release surface, locally reproduced: an embedded certified token (CERTIFIED_BY_FAKE_RELEASE_SUMMARY) bypassed the literal-match guard and polluted release/pointer/Markdown surfaces. The status is now allowlisted. Owner clean-streak count resets to 0.

V93 external review found two soundness findings, both locally reproduced: the exact-status note projected forged certified prose under status open, and forged placement-entry fields (plus a skipped public ghost_pick) could land in final_solution.json before later comparisons fired. Both fail closed now. Owner clean-streak count resets to 0.

V94 external review found one soundness finding, locally reproduced: surplus protocol storage boxes acted as occupancy blockers (removing them flipped the validator to layout_has_better_empty_rect). Excess boxes now fail closed. Owner clean-streak count resets to 0.

V95 external review found two soundness findings, both locally reproduced: forged operation_type metadata on optional entries and a forged note on last_stop_reason reached public artifacts while the surface stayed publishable. Both shapes are now closed. Owner clean-streak count resets to 0.

V96 external review found one soundness finding, locally reproduced: replacing data/preprocessed or data/solutions with a symlink served out-of-project artifacts under canonical names while the surface stayed publishable. All path components are now validated. Owner clean-streak count resets to 0.

V97 external review found one soundness finding, locally confirmed (the shipped regression fails on the unpatched tree, passes on the patched tree): a non-canonical shadow checkpoint published as CERTIFIED, and the inspector pre-resolved the campaign path so the V96 ancestry check missed a symlink alias. Authority is now pinned to the canonical checkpoint. Owner clean-streak count resets to 0.

V98 external review found one soundness finding, discrimination confirmed (regression fails unpatched, passes patched): the B5A wrapper resolved the campaign path before the central verifier, so a symlink alias reported b5a_certified_surface_publishable=True. The wrapper no longer pre-resolves. Owner clean-streak count resets to 0.

V99 seals the P1.2 close kernel: proof-bearing sink inventory, source_sha256 drift detection, guard-token checks, and explicit TCB/non-claim boundary. Owner clean-streak count remains outside the repo and P1.3 remains blocked.

2026-08-05 owner semantics adjudication (empty rectangle = nothing at all inside) changed the certified predicate (variant A on predicate 5), triggering the repair batch and reopening the close claim via source_sha256 drift. Three external review rounds converged to dual PASS_WITH_FINDINGS (F-03 closure confirmed twice, independently). The 2026-08-06 seal batch (a08ee02) closed the review-named hardening items and completed the reseal chain. Owner re-closed with the streak restarted from zero (count maintained outside the repo).

The I1 line added artifact-bound independent binding reverification and scope A mutation/anchor closure. Sink source_sha256 drift mechanically reopened P1.2; six external audit rounds found no soundness break and R6B concluded CLEAN_FOR_REOPEN. Owner approved re-close on 2026-08-21, retained the clean-review streak by discretion, accepted the historical allowlist id suffix _295, and authorized the narrow tracked companion. Stage-B alias semantics were reviewed before resealing, and the sealed-authority floor now matches final benders_loop.py bytes.
